newsitem.title: CANADA: Bridgewater sings Ella Fitzgerald in Montreal.
newsitem.headline: Bridgewater sings Ella Fitzgerald in Montreal.

text.p: Ella Fitzgerald, the venerated grande dame of jazz, was remembered in style at the Montreal International Jazz Festival on Thursday night in an energetic and elegant tribute by songstress Dee Dee Bridgewater.

Before a sold-out audience of 3,000 at the Place-des-Arts concert complex, Bridgewater displayed the qualities that have made her an instant crowd favorite since her first appearance at the festival in 1993.

The Memphis-born American vocalist and actress evoked the spirit of Fitzgerald, who died last year, with very personal renditions of classics such as "Undecided," "Stairway to the Stars" and "Lady Be Good."

From her explosive, body-twisting scatting on Duke Ellington's "Cottontail" through the comedic irony of "Mack The Knife" and her sensual come-hither entreaties on "Love For Sale," she revealed a range of musical expression that had the audience on its feet at the end of her first hour-long set.

Although appearing nervous at the start, perhaps overwhelmed by the adoring crowd's early outbursts of affection, Bridgewater settled in comfortably with her tight trio -- Thierry Eliez on piano, Thomas Bramerie on base and Andre Ceccarelli on drums.

The chanteuse, who lived in Paris for the past 11 years, also struck all the right notes by introducing most of her songs in English and lovely-accented French. That alone made her a honorary citizen of this French-speaking metropolis.

Bridgewater came back after a brief intermission dressed in a stunning body-hugging white evening gown and shawl, perfect attire to complement the white dinner jackets and blouses of her other musical collaborators for the evening -- the full Montreal Symphony Orchestra.

The second part of the show offered a glimpse of Bridgewater that is perhaps seldom seen elsewhere, her smooth and sultry side. Conductor John Clayton set the midsummer night tone with his composition "Three Shades of Blue," featuring local saxophone sensation Andre Leroux.
Clayton and Bridgewater then stole everyone's heart with lyrically romantic versions of "Autumn Leaves," sung in its original French, and "The Shadow of Your Smile," both arranged by Lalo Schifrin.

Bridgewater previewed her forthcoming album, a collaboration with Clayton paying homage to Fitzgerald, with four songs including Lionel Hampton's "Midnight Sun" and a heart-rending "My Heart Belongs to Daddy." Bridgewater's voice was pleadingly sweet, while Clayton used the MSO's string section to full effect on that last one.

For her encore after another standing ovation, the ethereal clarity of Bridgewater's voice came through on Ellington's "Come Sunday." Her prayer: "God of love, please, please look down and see my people through," was imbued with the sincerity of a singer who while turning with affection toward Fitzgerald, has much to say with her own voice.
The audience could not get enough, bringing her back for a curtain call, nor it seems could the camera crews, who were generously allowed to film much of the show.
